issues.message: Not yet placed by a builder GameTest: lily_of_the_valley, lectern, cornflower, oxeye_daisy, dandelion, candle, bell.
415 blocks, over the common budget of 350 (docs/STRUCTURES.md). A warning only.
13 layers tall: builders reach 9 without scaffolding, which isn't verified in game yet.
The roof does not reach past the walls on any two opposite sides: give it one block of overhang.

notes.artefacts: the standing lanterns at (4,4,0) and (6,4,0) sit on bottom-half stone brick stairs (facing west/east); a stair's top only covers half the block, so it can't hold a lantern and it drops in game. Put a full block, a top slab or a top-half stair under them, or hang them
notes.roof: Roof warning is a false alarm: 1-block overhang at both eaves and the back gable.
notes.life: Window flower boxes and front planters with flowers; no path yet.
notes.detail: Flower boxes, red runner, lectern, altar candles, chain-hung lanterns and a side bench give it real detail.

visual.summary: Level 2 adds the bell with its chain, trapdoor flower boxes under the side windows, front planters, a bench, a red aisle runner, a lectern, altar candles and lanterns inside and over the door.
problems: Lanterns at (4,4,0) and (6,4,0) stand on bottom stone_brick_stairs (door hood ends at (4,3,0) facing west and (6,3,0) facing east); a stair's top face has no centre support, so in game they pop off. Put them on a full block (e.g. make the hood ends stone bricks or top-half stairs) or hang them from a wall-side chain instead.
Reachability: interior floor, runner and pews are reached; unreached places are roofs, buttress caps, the outside flower boxes (window boxes, fine), the bell top and the gable slots. Fine.

notes.levels: Over L1, L2 adds the bell, flower beds along the plinth and at the door, two door lanterns, a bench, a red runner, lectern, candles and hung lanterns inside. The bell gives the cote its job, but from outside the step is still mostly props: L1 and L2 only tell apart up close. L3 is now clearly different (churchyard and lych gate), which answers Carlton's L2-vs-L3 note.
notes.detail: Capped at 1 under Carlton's rule: no clearly visible new feature from a distance at L2.
notes.artefacts: v1 problem fixed: door-hood lanterns at (4,4,4)/(6,4,4) now stand on top-half stone brick stairs (full top face). Gable shutters are open trapdoors on the outside wall beside the opening, not covering it.
notes.roof: Automatic overhang warning is a false alarm on the long sides (eaves overhang); the front gable is the bell-cote wall on purpose.

visual.summary: L2 furnishes the chapel: the bell in the cote, flower beds along the plinth and by the door, door lanterns, a bench, and inside a red runner, lectern, candles and hanging lanterns.
problems: Levels: L2 still differs from L1 mostly by small props (bell, flower beds, two lanterns). Add one feature that shows from a distance on top of L1, e.g. a small sacristy lean-to on one side wall, a covered side porch, or a lit notice board/bench with a roofed frame by the door (keep the churchyard in L3).
Reachability: interior floor, runner and pews are reached; unreached places are roofs, buttress caps, the outside flower boxes, the bell top and the gable slots. Fine.
